cities.d: (Мінск) — the Belarusian capital and largest city, with over 2 million inhabitants.

x.around: A single trip ticket for bus, tram or trolleybus is paper-based and costs 0.60 rubles if purchased from a ticket office or kiosk, 0.65 rubles if purchased from the driver (September 2019). Tickets have to be validated straight away. In metro, a single journey is 0.65 rubles (September 2019) paid by tokens bought at a window or self-service kiosk inside the station.

n.en: Ozertso - Open Air Museum of Rural Architecture and Life

hidden.d: 70-m-high mound from 1969 commemorating Soviet soldiers who died during World War II.
A small theatre well-regarded for its high-quality performances. Most of the plays are in Russian. Inexpensive tickets and unpretentious facilities.
A reconstructed line of defences on what once was the state border of the USSR.

This is a 750-mm (2 ft 5½ in) narrow gauge railway loop passing through the Chelyuskinites Park. The railway line counts 3 stations (listed from north to south): Zaslonovo, Pionerskaya (or Pionerskaja) and Sosnovy Bor (or…

x.intro: Minsk (Belarusian: Мінск, Russian: Минск) is the capital and largest city of the Republic of Belarus. Its population is about two million people in 2024.

must.d: Huge, glass and concrete rhombicuboctahedron houses a collection of over 8 million items. On 22 floors it features conference halls, 20 reading rooms and a Book Museum, on the roof there is an observation deck with good views of…

Huge trucks and super heavy-duty hauliers are produced in Žodzina, a town in Minsk region. The manufacturing site is open for visits to see the world’s largest trucks listed in the Guinness Book of Records.
The best-known church in the city, commonly known as the Red Church (or Čyrvony kasciol), was built between 1908 and 1910 in Romanesque Revival style.

n.de: Kirche des heiligen Simon und der heiligen Helena (Minsk)
n.en: St Simon and St Helena Church
n.es: iglesia de los Santos Simón y Elena

must.d: One of the most popular tourist destinations in Minsk. It offers an excellent overview of fine arts in Belarus. Many art description tags are in English. The main collection is spread across two buildings.

n.es: Museo Nacional de Arte de Bielorrusia
n.fr: musée national des Beaux-Arts de Biélorussie
n.it: Museo nazionale di belle arti della Repubblica di Bielorussia

must.d: The main Orthodox church of Belarus, a fine example of the late baroque style, known in Belarus as Vilno baroque. It was built in 1633-1642 as a Roman Catholic church of the Bernardine monastery.
Built as a Jesuit church at the beginning of the 18th century, this beautiful Baroque church was closed or used as a sports training facility during different periods of the Soviet Union time.

n.en: Archcathedral of the Name of the Most Holy Virgin Mary
n.es: Catedral de la Santa Virgen María

must.d: A place where a village, savagely massacred in 1943 by Nazi forces, once stood.
A large collection of exhibits about WWII in Belarus.

n.de: Museum des Großen Vaterländischen Krieges in Minsk
n.es: Museo estatal bielorruso de la Gran Guerra Patriótica
n.fr: musée d'Histoire de la Grande Guerre nationale de Biélorussie
n.it: Museo nazionale bielorusso della storia della Grande guerra patriottica

next.d: is a regional capital on the border with Poland and is rich with history from both the Soviet times and before.
is a border town in north-west Belarus, the last capital of Rzecz Pospolita, the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth in 17-18th centuries.

x.safe: Minsk is a safe and clean city. If you are in need of assistance, there is a strong police presence in the downtown area. Emergency medical help can be accessed 24/7, either in designated hospitals or by phone.

cities.d: (Брэст) — regional capital on the Polish border with impressive architectural sights.

x.around: Transport within Brest city is very regular, with many different bus routes through the city, and also regular trolley-buses through the city. Taxis are also easy to order and "marshrutkas" also operate throughout the city. The main attractions are all within walking distance.

hidden.d: A very beautiful train station, both from outside and from inside.

x.intro: Brest (Belarusian: Брэст; Russian: Брест) is a border town in the south-west corner of Belarus, near Terespol in Poland. Brest is a city closely linked to the history of Central and Eastern Europe and the ever-changing borders. One aspect of the city that shows this is its architecture, with parts of Brest quite Polish in character. However the eastern links are also strong, with beautiful orthodox churches and some prime examples of Soviet building styles.

must.d: A complex of massive fortification built in mid-19th century by the Russian Empire. In November 1918 the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was signed here.

An incredible collection of impressive locomotives from the Soviet era. While there is not much effort in the presentation (they are all displayed one after the other), the variety of the locomotives and carriages is impressive.

next.d: is the Belarusian Lviv, an old and beautiful town north from Brest. By bus it's some four hours and .
(Belavezhskaya Pushcha) is an ancient woodland straddling the border between Belarus and Poland, located 70 north from Brest.

n.it: Parco nazionale della foresta di Białowieża

next.d: is just a few kilometers away. There is one dedicated daily train from Brest to Warsaw, departing at 15:23 Belarusian time, reaching Warsaw at 17:25 Polish time.

x.safe: Belarus has a low rate of crime, and the atmosphere is mostly very friendly even on big celebrations (when everyone is drunk).

cities.d: (Полацк Polack) — the oldest Belarusian city, notable for interesting buildings.

hidden.d: The collection includes some rare 16th-century editions. The building. It was erected in the 18th century as a monastery school.

x.intro: Polotsk (or Polatsk) is a city in Belarus, in Vitebsk Oblast. First mentioned in 862, it is the oldest city in Belarus. Now it is a city of local importance with 83,000 inhabitants (2009) and with considerable architectural heritage from the times of old Rus and later periods.

must.d: This medieval building was completely redecorated during the Baroque period.
A well-preserved building from the times of old Rus', with some later alterations.

cities.d: (Гомель Homiel) — the second largest city in Belarus; located in the east.

hidden.d: Beautiful neoclassical building with interior decorated in 19th-century spirit and a dominating Lenin statue on the stairs to the upper floors.
Very nice bridge over river Sosz with the wide views on the nearby beaches and Gomel Palace. In front of bridge is a monument to a fisherman on a boat.
A park with marble statues, chapel, winter garden and the Neoclassical church of Sts. Peter and Paul. An image of the residence was featured on the old 20,000-ruble bill.

x.intro: Gomel (Belarusian/Russian: Го́мель; also transliterated Homieĺ based on the Belarusian pronunciation) is the second largest city in Belarus (around 500 000 inhabitants), and is the capital of Gomel Oblast.

cities.d: (Пінск) — informally known as the capital of Belarusian Polesie (Pinsk, or Pripyat, Marshes).

hidden.d: Large complex built between 1635–48 in Mannerist style. Today houses a school and a museum.

n.en: Buildings of the former Jesuit college

x.intro: Pinsk is a city in Belarus in Brest Oblast located at the confluence of the Pina and Prypiat rivers. First mentioned in 1097, it enjoyed reasonable local importance for centuries, being at different times a seat of Orthodox bishops, a location of a big Jesuit college, and home for a thriving Jewish community. Today it has a population of around 130,000.

cities.d: (Гродна Hrodna) — the last capital city of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (18th cent.) with rich history and well-preserved architecture.

x.around: There are plenty of buses and trolley buses going around town. In the evenings though, they get down to travelling on the outskirts once an hour or two. A ticket for a trip costs 0.13 rubles. Buy the tickets from kiosks near the bus stops. If you speak no Russian, just say "Talony," and hold up fingers to indicate how many.

hidden.d: The present appearance of this royal residence was mostly shaped in 16th century, when it was renovated in Renaissance fashion for King Stephen Bathory. Only a few elements of the previous Gothic castle survive.
The old Fire Tower built at the end of 19th century. Every day at midday a trumpeter dressed in historic costume goes 120 stairs up and plays a tune on the top of the tower.

x.intro: Grodno (Belarusian: Гродна Hrodna, Russian: Гродно Grodno) is a city in Belarus, on the Neman River, close to the borders of Poland and Lithuania (about 20 km and 30 km away respectively).

must.d: A fine Baroque basilica, once a church of a Jesuit monastery, now the city's Roman Catholic cathedral.
A 12th-century Orthodox church, one of the few surviving monuments of the Old Rus period in the country.

n.fr: église Saints-Boris-et-Gleb de Hrodna de Kaloja

must.d: Hrodna Zoo is next to the railway station. It was the first Belarusian Zoo, opened in 1927. There are over 300 kinds of animals in the Zoo nowadays: predators, small predators, hoofed animals, birds and a terrarium.

x.safe: Grodno is a safe city, resembling its Polish counterparts much more than you would probably expect.

cities.d: (Магілёў Magiliow) — third largest city in Belarus.

x.around: Local transportation system includes buses, trolleys and minibuses (marshrutkas). They are quite cheap: buses and trolleys in March 2008 were roughly US$0.25, and minibuses were around US$0.40. Cabs prices can be quite different, especially they might be expensive for not fluent in Russian language travelers.

must.d: The city's Catholic cathedral where parishioners will often be singing. The original frescoes survived World War II remarkably well. It is very beautiful inside.

n.es: Concatedral de la Asunción de la Virgen y San Estanislao
n.it: cattedrale dell'Assunzione di Maria Vergine e San Stanislao

must.d: The 1668 Cathedral dome is being restored and the iconostasis and frescos are magnificent inside. Outside the nuns tend beautiful flower gardens and a variety of apple trees.
One of the most interesting landmarks of the town. Rebuilt in 2008.
Masterpiece of constructivism, built in 1935, looks like House of Parliament in Minsk. Located on the Lenin Square with Lenin monument.

A war memorial chiefly to the World War II soldiers and civilians who defended the city for 23 days in July 1941 when Belarus was part of the USSR. Few survived, it's estimated 82,000 Russians and 30,000 Germans perished.
Main square of the city. Good city view. Location of the Town hall with small museum inside.

x.safe: In general Mogilev, like the rest of Belarus, is very safe. Just exercise the usual precautions. The people of Mogilev are kind and hospitable. They are interested in where you come from and your culture.

cities.d: (Нясвіж Niasviž) — with a UNESCO listed castle.

must.d: UNESCO World Heritage Site, a residential castle of the Radziwiłł family since the 16th century.
A magnificent building from 1584–1593, one of the first Baroque churches in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. Many members of the Radziwiłł family are buried here.
A building with Renaissance and Baroque features, one of not so many preserved city halls in Belarus
An old city gate constructed around 1700, which takes its name from the nearby city of Slutsk

next.d: ly around 27 km away, is home to another UNESCO World Heritage site. It is possible to do both sites in one day by bus. Bus leaves Nesvizh at 14:26 and arrives at Mir at 15:05.

cities.d: (Віцебск Vitsyebsk) — the city of Marc Chagall.

x.around: Buses, trolleybuses, and trams all operate in and around the city, and cost in the area of US$0.40 for a single ride. Monthly passes are also available should you have an extended stay. Private buses and "route taxis" also operate throughout the city, for higher rates, but are more likely to be available and run punctually.

hidden.d: A beautiful example of old wooden style Orthodox churches.

x.intro: Vitebsk or Viciebsk (Belarusian: Віцебск, Russian: Витебск) is the middle of Vitebsk Oblast in Belarus.

must.d: A Romanesque Revival church.

n.es: Catedral de Santa Bárbara y San Pablo

must.d: With its renowned clock tower, it is a beautiful piece of 18th century architecture.

x.safe: Belarusians are typically quite friendly to foreigners, sometimes too much, however. Some less scrupulous individuals get tourists drunk and then rob them. Western men are advised that attentive females encountered in dancing clubs and bars are highly likely to be con artists.

intro: Belarus (Belarusian and Russian: Белару́сь) is a former Soviet state whose history begins in the 10th century CE. While not on most tourists' radar, Belarus preserves beautiful castles, pristine nature, and Soviet heritage. It maintains close ties and an open border with its neighbor Russia.

other.d: (Нацыянальны парк Белавежская пушча, Natsyyanal’ny park Byelavyezhskaya pushcha) — on the border with Poland, this primeval forest is a

n.it: Parco nazionale della foresta di Białowieża

x.around: The National Park Headquarters at Kamieniuki has a zoo and a museum.
x.intro: Belovezhskaya Pushcha National Park (Belarusian: Белавежская пушча) is in the Brest and Hrodna regions of Belarus.

x.around: Mir is a rather small town and it will take you about 10-15 minutes to walk to the Mir Castle from the middle of the town where the bus stop is located. The bus stop is in Market Square - where the local market, a bank and a hotel can be found.
x.intro: Mir is a town in the Kareličy region of Grodno Oblast in Belarus. Prior to the 2nd World War it was known as an international centre of Jewish learning (Mir yeshiva).

must.d: This late medieval castle is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The ticket into the castle and the chapel-crypt behind it can be bought at the entrance - 100 m away from the castle gate tower.

next.d: around 27 km away, is home to another UNESCO World Heritage site. It is possible to do both sites in one day. There is a bus from Nesvizh at 14:26 which arrives at Mir at 15:05.
